units.selection_reason: Torus-fixed subschemes become monomial ideals and three-dimensional partitions; outgoing two-dimensional partitions determine a unique minimal Cohen-Macaulay support, while extra finite length measures deviation from it. Stable pairs with that support are then recast as finite-length invariant submodules of an explicit quotient module. The comparison reveals a structural change: combinatorial fixed subschemes are isolated, but fixed submodules can form positive-dimensional components whose Euler characteristics enter the count.
units.title: Translate torus-fixed geometry into asymptotic partitions and finite-length module subobjects
